## Mixed spatial review

The current renderer keeps 2D images facing the camera under yaw and pitch, using shared upright virtual depth for lighting/picking while bodies and shadow proxies remain world-space. Shadow-only casters do not occupy color layers; proxy geometry, reveal uniforms and plank detail are reused. Native visual acquisition is observer-private; the designated introduction selector admits only the observer's own acquisition, not private thoughts or third-party evidence. Indexed route-support projection, crossed-cell terrain checks and worker failure/shutdown handling are implemented. [Evidence](../../docs/verification/mixed-spatial-review.md) and SW/EPR/PF/SR trackers separate these facts from unqualified GPU, crowd, exposure and lifecycle limits.
The client has camera-facing lit sprites with separate upright virtual depth beside meshes, sun/local-fire lighting, multi-receiver shadow maps with simple body proxies, continuous right-drag orbit/pitch and profile-configurable local authorized read-through. Ramp display interpolation preserves common seams; cutaway geometry retains shadows. The target-only reveal pass does not open holes onto unknown background content. This is not full per-pixel occluder-opacity editing or inferred 3D art.
Current facts: [Architecture](../../docs/architecture.md#spatial-world-foundation). Current observations: [Recast integration](../../docs/verification/recast-integration.md). [SW](../../docs/maintainers/spatial-world.md) retains incomplete tile-update, sliding-controller, crowd, flight-graph, exposure-delta, viewport, model-loader and sustained graphics/load work. Earlier lattice benchmarks are historical. No automated suites were run for this delivery.

An external physical occurrence and an individual observer acquiring evidence are distinct. The [private-acquisition boundary](../../docs/events-perception-and-reactions.md#4-scope-and-event-identity) owns their scope and identity.
Cross-consumer and private-acquisition coverage belongs to [EPR03](../../docs/maintainers/events-perception-and-reactions.md#epr03--actor-private-perception-acquisition-and-exposure-deltas) and [EPR09](../../docs/maintainers/events-perception-and-reactions.md#epr09--differential-and-performance-acceptance); sensory correctness remains here.

Current runtime refinements use indexed support candidates during physical corridor projection and supercover ground-cell traversal during continuous displacement. They do not add placement snapping or use navigation rays for sensing. The [navigation failure/shutdown contract](../../docs/performance.md#navigation-failure-and-shutdown) owns bounded worker launch, retirement and publication failure handling; [world presentation](../../docs/world-presentation.md#motion-and-depth) owns full camera-facing artwork with separate virtual depth and physical bodies. Initial visual acquisitions use observer-private evidence; richer EPR exposure transitions remain separately tracked.

Static queries retain full-extent immutable indexes, frozen-stance/pose memoization, geometry/sense invalidation, range-first hearing and ordered acoustic transmission. Landing uses phase-local occupied extents, not general crowd arbitration. Senses never call a navmesh walkability raycast. Current body-authorized entities remain the disclosure boundary. EPR03's initial visual acquisition is observer-private; richer exposure deltas and D51's multi-view/viewport work remain open.
`WorldRenderer` keeps PlayCanvas out of simulation and protocol. [World presentation](world-presentation.md) owns current arbitrary camera movement, fully camera-facing lit sprites with separate upright depth, actual mesh/proxy shadows, configurable local authorized read-through and picking. Right-drag orbits yaw/pitch; primary/middle drag pans. Recast does not determine drawing order or camera sight. Camera cutaways retain physical/acoustic/shadow geometry; the read-through pass redraws authorized hidden target fragments rather than making holes onto unknown background content.
`projectAttributes` supplies applicable values, actual ranges/units and permitted concerns to the HUD, public entity inspection, owner inspection and decision context. Public entity projection omits owner-only attributes; the native actor observation strips sparse state from other actors. The existing native urgency thresholds remain distinct from context and meter thresholds. Additional need crossings emit owner-private `attribute-concern` evidence through the existing event/awareness path, with a saved hysteresis flag and a recovery margin of 5% of the configured range. Private attribute concerns remain excluded from narrator selection. ActorWork observes concern bands, not each quantity revision; the general EPR episode service, dirty intake and reminders remain unimplemented.
Native encounter projection captures position scalars once after movement and uses stable spatial candidates for people and objects. Prior visibility membership uses sets; unchanged visibility arrays retain identity. Native visual acquisition goes through `recordVisualAcquisition` and the existing ledger/experience owner, with only the observer in its private audience and observed modality. Sleepers acquire no new visual evidence. Living-source entry keeps its existing cognition importance; ordinary object entry does not force a cognition call. The story selector permits a designated introduction from the viewer's own sole-recipient visual acquisition, while excluding private thoughts and other actors' evidence. External speech/action events still resolve their actual event-time audiences; acquisition is no longer an audience-resolver cache consumer. Richer exposure deltas and encounter hysteresis remain EPR work. Cognitive signature refresh has separate `cognition.thoughtRefresh` and `cognition.maintenanceRefresh` spans. `ActorWork` still visits all memory-capable minds; thought signatures compute nearby visibility before readiness selection. Autonomous admission still has one world-global workflow and a default 45-second global thought interval, in addition to actor cooldowns. This limits many-agent responsiveness independently of native tick speed.

The current rendering adapter shares billboard depth/CPU picking transforms, removes shadow-only proxies from color layers, batches decorative plank seams and reuses reveal uniforms. Navigation support projection queries only spatially relevant candidate surfaces. A supercover terrain traversal checks every crossed terrain cell, including short diagonal water crossings; continuous coordinates remain independent of that representation. Worker failure and shutdown rules are in [performance](performance.md#navigation-failure-and-shutdown).

## Camera-facing sprites and mixed spatial review

Superseded upright-only Y-billboards with fully camera-facing artwork and separate virtual depth, without rotating mechanical bodies or shadow proxies. Recorded color-pass-free shared shadow proxies, batched plank detail, reveal uniform reuse, indexed corridor projection, exact terrain-cell crossings and worker failure/shutdown boundaries. Completed EPR03's initial private visual-acquisition scope correction and preserved the viewer's designated introduction; retained broader EPR exposure work. Updated obsolete audience-cache regression work and added SR21–SR23. Mixed browser/application observations and adverse limits belong in their evidence record, not a scale-certification claim.

Preserve and qualify the implemented phase-local scalar spatial candidate pass for object encounters and unchanged visibility-array identity. Initial visual acquisition has only the observer as its private recipient, so it needs no external audience resolver. Each record still commits through the existing mutation owner. Complete general external-event candidate reuse, exact event-time validity, exposure deltas and differential acceptance; external audiences cannot be reused across movement, life/sleep or sense changes. Do not recreate the old full-scan-to-grid rewrite or treat these delivered subsets as complete EPR02/EPR03 delivery.

- [ ] **SR10 — Observer-private acquisition and introductions:** cover separate observers acquiring the same source, sleepers/dead/non-memory actors, private contacts interleaved with visual entries, reentry, same-version restore, removal and source/sense changes. Only the visual observer receives the acquisition; seeing the observer does not reveal its hidden target. Preserve native living-entry reconsideration and the observer's designated-story milestone, while rejecting third-party/private-thought/disabled-policy narration and avoiding automatic stories for ordinary objects. Ordinary speech/actions still use current event-time audiences. Compare each observer's own valid entries, not the obsolete external acquisition audience or its removed cache.

## Mixed spatial review — additional qualification

The [mixed review evidence](../verification/mixed-spatial-review.md) records builds and actual runtime/browser observations, not completed automated regression gates.

- [ ] **SR21 — Full-facing sprite and depth equivalence:** sample yaw/pitch/projection after an actual rendered frame; camera matrices can lag a command until rendering. Compare visible image aspect, feathered reveal, virtual-body depth, alpha picking, status anchors and world-stable shadow orientation. Include camera-close and near-plane cases, negative scale/facing, bob/animation, cutout versus blended/remembered art and overlapping eligible targets. Shader compilation alone is not visual correctness; neither may camera rotation change physical collision or bodily sensing.
- [ ] **SR22 — Shadow/reveal resource lifetime and cost:** assert shadow-only proxies never enter color/depth color-pass lists, including hierarchy toggles, floor focus and observed-to-remembered transitions. Remove all instances/rebuild repeatedly with retained shared proxy geometry; verify balanced mesh/material ownership and correct shadows after recreation. Exercise many receivers/lights and all reveal modes, texture replacement/disposal and zero-strength/revocation paths. Measure actual GPU/pass work; draw-count reduction is not an FPS guarantee.
- [ ] **SR23 — Spatial query/worker boundaries:** compare indexed corridor candidates against complete support enumeration, including stacked and partly overlapping ramps and tolerance edges. Compare terrain-cell supercover against independent crossing calculations for zero/short/reversed/diagonal paths and grid boundaries; do not require position quantization. Exercise dispatch failure, clean worker exit, concurrent store failure/publication/retirement/close, stale load results and bounded retry behavior. Qualify source admission and native time preservation without replacing the existing world writer.
